name: guardian_prompt_report
description: The prompt of the report step: the rules every call follows and the schema of each of its three calls (core, story, close), plus the one-line repair request. Read by GuardianReportBuild, which has a built-in copy.
data:
{"rules": "You write the structured report of a FINISHED Guardian security investigation. You get the task the investigation was given, the EVIDENCE (the run's tool results, each numbered t1, t2, ...), the investigation's CONCLUSION and the TOOLS the run could call. Return ONE JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no Markdown.

Rules:
- Use only facts that appear in the EVIDENCE or the CONCLUSION. Never invent a host, user, IP, domain, hash, process, time or technique. Copy values exactly as written. If there is nothing for a section, return an empty list.
- "ref" lists the evidence ids that show the item (for example ["t2"]). The CONCLUSION is not evidence: a fact found only in the conclusion gets "ref": [].
- An entity is a concrete identifier copied from the evidence: a user name, host name, process image, file name or path, IP address, domain, URL, email address, hash or cloud resource id. A generic word ("workstation", "server", "attacker", "malware") or a label ("suspicious file") is never an entity.
- Times are ISO 8601 UTC, taken from the evidence only.
- Strings are plain text, short, no HTML or Markdown. Respect every list cap.
- The verdict, confidence and severity of the report come from the run's own record. Do not return them.
- An action's "cmd" may only name a command from the TOOLS list. When no listed command fits, leave "cmd" out. Never propose an action about Guardian's own bookkeeping (Guardian incident fields, case notes, memory, or the verdict itself).
", "core": "Return exactly these keys:
{"v":1,
 "headline": str<=140 (one sentence: what happened and how sure),
 "entities": [<=20 {"id":"e1","type": user|host|process|file|ip|domain|url|email|hash|cloud|other, "value": str<=120,
              "rep": malicious|suspicious|benign|unknown, "role": victim|attacker|infra|asset|tool|other, "ref":[ids]}],
 "edges": [<=30 {"from":"e1","to":"e2","rel": logged_on|ran|spawned|wrote|connected|resolved|downloaded|sent|received|
            authenticated|accessed|other, "time"?: iso, "ref":[ids]}]   ("from REL to", e.g. a process connected to an ip)
}", "story": "Return exactly these keys:
{"v":1,
 "attack": [<=15 {"tactic": ATT&CK enterprise tactic name, "tech": "T1071.001", "name": str<=60, "time"?: iso,
            "evidence": str<=160, "ents": [entity ids], "ref":[ids]}]   (only techniques the evidence shows),
 "timeline": [<=25 {"t": iso, "event": str<=160, "src": str<=24 (data source), "ents": [entity ids], "tech"?: str,
              "ref":[ids]}]   (only events with a time in the evidence),
 "tree": [<=30 {"id":"n1","parent": "n0"|null, "ent"?: entity id, "name": str<=60, "cmd"?: str<=160, "pid"?: str,
          "flag"?: malicious|suspicious, "tech"?: str, "ref":[ids]}]   (the process tree, only if the evidence has one)
}
Use the entity ids already defined (listed below); do not create new entities.", "close": "Return exactly these keys:
{"v":1,
 "findings": [<=10 {"text": str<=200, "ref":[ids]}]   (the key facts, each tied to its evidence),
 "actions": [<=8 {"p": 1|2|3, "action": str<=160, "owner": "guardian"|"analyst", "approval": true|false,
             "cmd"?: str<=200}]   (approval true for anything that changes a system; "cmd" only from the TOOLS list),
 "gaps": [<=5 str<=200]   (what the investigation could not establish)
}", "repair": "Return only the JSON object."}
